claim_1.claim: CyTOF analysis of peripheral immune cells from 64 COVID-19 patients and 12 healthy controls showed depletion of CD16 monocytes, dendritic cells, and NK cells, as well as increases in plasmablasts in patients with severe and fatal COVID-19.

sources.quote: We saw similar trends in immune cell composition between the three modalities, including depletion of CD16 monocytes, dendritic cells (DCs), and NK cells, as well as increases in plasmablasts (PBs) in patients with severe and fatal COVID-19.

comparison.finding: depletion of CD16 monocytes, dendritic cells, and NK cells, and increases in plasmablasts in severe COVID-19

claim_2.claim: CyTOF analysis of NK cells from COVID-19 patients and healthy controls showed increased expression of the activation markers CD38 and CD69, and death receptor ligand FasL.

sources.quote: peripheral NK cells were substantially depleted across all three modalities, although the frequencies of CD56bright, CD56dim, and CD56− NK cells as a percentage of all NK cells did not change (Fig. 6, A and B).

increased expression of the activation markers CD38 and CD69, and we also demonstrate that surface expression of the death receptor ligand FasL is increased in moderate and severe COVID-19 patients (Fig. 6, E and F).

comparison.finding: frequencies of CD56bright, CD56dim, and CD56− NK cells as a percentage of all NK cells did not change; increased expression of the activation markers CD38 and CD69, andthe death receptor ligand FasL in moderate and severe COVID-19 patients
